slides.0.title: Grapes and Base Wine
slides.0.subtitle: Why high-acid, low-alcohol white wine suits distillation
slides.1.title: What makes a good base wine
slides.1.highlights.0.title: High acidity
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Sulphur dioxide is not allowed in Cognac, so Ugni Blanc's high acidity protects the wine before distillation (Difford's Guide)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Low alcohol
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Low alcohol concentrates aroma and gives more delicate, floral spirits (Martell); Difford's Guide notes most houses avoid distilling wine above 9.5%
slides.1.highlights.2.title: No sugar, no sulphite
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sugar and sulphites are strictly prohibited during Cognac fermentation, which uses wild yeast; only wine of the latest harvest may be distilled (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.1.content: Sources differ on base-wine strength and fermentation times, so only the shared concepts are used.
slides.2.title: Cognac's varieties
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Ugni Blanc
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Known locally as Saint-Émilion, it dominates; Martell describes it as high-yielding, late-ripening, low in alcohol, high in acid and disease-resistant (shares range from over 90% to over 98% by source)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Folle Blanche
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The main variety before phylloxera, it is now under 1% of plantings (Martell)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Other permitted varieties
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Colombard is high in acid and low in sugar; Montils ripens earlier; Folignan, a cross of Ugni Blanc and Folle Blanche, was added to the specification in 2005 (Martell)
slides.2.content: The Cognac specification requires the main varieties to total at least 90% (Wikipedia).
slides.3.title: Varieties elsewhere
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Armagnac
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Ten varieties are permitted but four dominate: Ugni Blanc, Baco, Folle Blanche and Colombard; Baco (Baco 22A) is a hybrid, which the WSET Level 2 guide calls the only hybrid authorised in any European AOC system
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Spain
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Brandy de Jerez uses Airén and Palomino and a solera system; Brandy del Penedès uses Parellada, Folle Blanche and Ugni Blanc (vinetur)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Shares differ by source
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Ugni Blanc's share in Armagnac is 55% in alcademics but about 50% in the WSET Level 2 guide, so it is not tested
slides.3.content: A variety's role is not to taste good but to suit distillation.
